messages:
deploybot: ALERT: rollout 2.9.1 -> embeddings-route triggered safety rule. p95 latency +22% over baseline (5m). Recommendation: auto-rollback. https://deploys.redwood.internal/r/2.9.1
maya (eng-release): hmm, errors are flat, just latency. Canary traffic is 7%. any config flips? :thinking_face:
kevin (sre): saw a small model quantization tweak in the canary config 10:12 UTC. that could nudge seq-latency. pulling logs now.
jess (pm): we just shipped a release note blurb. need to decide fast — customers on dedicated pools? any risk to embeddings accuracy if we revert?
maya (eng-release): accuracy looks the same on our quick eval set. but p95 jump is real on small batch sizes. I prefer partial rollback for embeddings route only, not whole service.
oncall-alex: I'm on it. if we do partial rollback, we should pin traffic to 0% for the canary and route new requests to 2.9.0 for embeddings.
kevin (sre): pre-rollback checklist: snapshot index, announce maintenance, run health-checks post-cutover. I'll trigger the incident bridge.
ops-bridge-bot: Created incident INC-1234: "embeddings p95 drift during 2.9.1 canary" and opened bridge https://ops.redwood.internal/bridge/INC-1234
maya (eng-release): command to pin back to 2.9.0 for embeddings (50% traffic initially):
```
rwctl rollback --service embeddings --to-version 2.9.0 --traffic 50 --reason "p95 latency regression in canary"
```
kevin (sre): i'll run the command in 2m. will watch p95 and error rate. if p95 improves and errors steady, we'll do staged traffic shift to 100% over 10m.
jess (pm): I'll draft a short customer note, cc: enterprise-customers, explaining brief routing change and that model behavior is unchanged.
oncall-alex: Executing rollback now. taking snapshot first. ping me if anything odd. :eyes:
deploybot: ACTION: rollback command accepted for release 2.9.1 -> embeddings route. status: started.
maya (eng-release): thanks team. post-rollback next steps: update release notes to mention staged routing fix, and schedule a follow-up retro tomorrow. :thumbsup:"
